body:
Stacked on #5358 (its two commits are part of this diff until it merges; then this PR shrinks to the last three commits). Draft until then.

## What
The non-const `operator[](json_pointer)` now has the **strong exception guarantee**: if resolving the pointer throws (`out_of_range`, `bad_alloc`, `length_error` while padding an array, ...), the value is unchanged. Previously, values created for earlier reference tokens stayed behind. Found in the compliance review of JSON Pointer (RFC 6901).

- Rollback via a small RAII guard (no try/catch, so it also works with `JSON_NOEXCEPTION`); it reverts by iterator, so it does not allocate or convert keys.
- `get_unchecked` is a non-inserting walk; creation moved to a never-inlined `get_unchecked_create`, which keeps the hot read path faster than before.
- Object types whose lookup and `emplace()` disagree (copied `fifo_map`) no longer hit an assert/crash; such pointers throw `out_of_range.404` and leave the value unchanged.
- Creating values no longer needs `string_t::begin()` (compiles with the alternative string type of the tests).
- Documentation of `operator[]` states the guarantee and the requirement for custom template parameters.

## Performance
Cachegrind instruction counts (GCC 16 / clang 22, C++11/17) and Apple clang, 14 rows: no row is slower than the base (#5358 merged with develop); most are 2–33 % faster.

## Breaking changes
No breaking changes to the public API. Behavioural change: a failing `operator[](json_pointer)` now leaves the value untouched instead of leaving partially created values (an exception-safety improvement, was undocumented before).

It is there on purpose, though not as a measured saving: `undo()` is `JSON_HEDLEY_NEVER_INLINE`, so a `case change::none` in its `switch` would make every successful access call an out-of-line function just to do nothing. With the inlined check, the success path contains no call at all; I checked the `-O2` assembly of `j[ptr]`, where the only call to `undo()` is in the unwind cleanup block. I did not benchmark the alternative.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Right, no reason. `resize(m_old_size)` shrinks the array exactly as the `erase` did and avoids the `difference_type` cast. Changed in e1aa393226. I ran the rollback tests with `std::vector` and `std::deque` as `array_t`; both leave the value unchanged after a failing access.

Good question; it turns out not to be needed. I built a variant where the destructor calls `undo()` unconditionally and `undo()` is no longer `JSON_HEDLEY_NEVER_INLINE` (the `none` case is already in the `switch`), and compared it against the previous version with an A/B harness (both in one binary, several code layouts):

- GCC 13 `-O3` on Linux: instructions per repetition are identical for `j[ptr]` on existing paths, a one-token access, and creating paths (ratio 1.00000). Timings are within noise (geomean 1.000 / 0.98 / 1.001).
- clang `-O2` on macOS: instruction ratios 0.99998 / 1.00008 / 1.0039; timings within noise.

clang still keeps the single `undo()` call in the unwind cleanup and inlines the "nothing to do" test itself, and GCC's output got slightly smaller. So I took your suggestion: simplified in 9b8e5f848b.

I did not measure branch mispredictions separately.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*
